doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: Growing up in Chicago with musician parents; starting trumpet
summary: Both parents were musicians; Gardner took piano, then at nine insisted on trumpet and got one from his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That’s great. Well you grew up in Chicago.
And was there a point, a definite point in your life that you said music, that’s it for me; that’s going to be my career.

Yeah. As a matter of fact it’s funny, I just answered that question earlier today in Doc’s history class. And it was around the time when I was about maybe a junior in high school that I said I think music is the direction I’m going to go. Both my parents are musicians and educators as well. My father is a jazz trumpeter and he was in the Ray Charles band back in the early sixties, with Hank Crawford and Marcus Belgrade and all those guys, and “Fathead” Newman. And my mother is a classical pianist and organist and choir director. So growing up in Chicago I kind of got it from both ends. You know my mother would be practicing the classical music upstairs, and then down in the basement was my father’s practice room and he’d be swinging, playing Cannonball. And I was taking piano lessons at five years old. My mother had me take piano lessons, and practicing these very simple beginning piano etudes or whatever. And I eventually got bored with it, after three or four years of doing it. And I finally decided upon, after hearing my father’s music, I said “I want to play that.” You know, “you want to play jazz?” “Yeah, I want to do that.” I didn’t know the piano could do that. You know? And so my elementary school started a band program and I was nine years old. And they said “who wants to join the band?” And I said “I want to join the band.” And they said “what do you want to play?” “I want to play the trumpet.” “Well we don’t have a trumpet, what about this clarinet over here?” “No, trumpet.” They said “well we don’t have a trumpet.” So I said “I’ll take care of this.” So I ran home and said, “Daddy, I want to play the trumpet.” “Really?” So he had a trumpet for me. So I showed up the next day with a trumpet. You know and the rest is kind of history I guess.
